meta.titre: HTML Tags: building a web page with the basic tags
meta.sous_theme: Structure of an HTML page and the roles of the basic tags

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A cyber cafe owner in Limbe wants a simple web page announcing her opening hours. She does not need special software: a text editor and a browser are enough, because a web page is only text with tags that tell the browser what to show. The GCE asks two kinds of questions on this topic. In the multiple-choice paper you name the tag that does a job, and in the written paper you describe the role of a tag or write a short piece of code. Knowing each basic tag and its closing partner earns those marks easily.

items: A web browser is a program, such as Chrome or Firefox, used to display web pages.
A text editor such as Notepad can be used to type and save plain text.
A file name has an extension after the dot, such as .html, which shows the type of file.

sections.titre: The structure of a page and the basic tags
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What HTML is **HTML** (HyperText Markup Language) is the language used to describe the content of a web page. It is a *markup* language, not a programming language: it labels text so that a web browser knows how to display it. An HTML file is plain text saved with the extension .html or .htm and opened in a browser. ### Tags A **tag** is an instruction written between angle brackets. variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for bullets or numbers
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Choose `
    ` for bullets or `
      ` for numbers, put each item between `
    1. ` and `
      2. `, and close the list with the matching tag. The browser adds the bullets or the numbers by itself.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the page must connect to another page or show a picture
variantes.contenu_markdown: A link is written `text`: the text between the tags is clickable and the address goes in the href attribute. A picture is written ``; it is an empty tag, so it has no closing tag.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When data must appear in rows and columns
variantes.contenu_markdown: `<table>` wraps the table, `<tr>` makes a row, `<th>` makes a heading cell and `<td>` makes an ordinary cell. The number of cells is the number of rows times the number of cells in each row.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the HTML code for a web page that has: the title *Class Notice* in the browser tab, the main heading *Class 5 Trip*, the paragraph *We leave at 7 am.*, a horizontal line, and then a numbered list of three items: *Bring water*, *Wear shoes* and *Be on time*.

etapes.action: Write the frame of the page.
etapes.justification: Every page is wrapped in html, with a head and a body.

etapes.action: Put the title in the head.
etapes.justification: The title tag belongs in the head because it is shown on the browser tab and not in the page itself.

etapes.action: Add the heading and the paragraph to the body.
etapes.justification: The main heading is the largest level, h1, and the sentence is a paragraph, p.
hr draws the line and is an empty tag, so it is written alone.
Numbers need ol, and each item needs li, with every tag closed.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
The complete code is: ``` Class Notice

Class 5 Trip

We leave at 7 am.

  1. Bring water
  2. Wear shoes
  3. Be on time
``` The browser shows the heading, the sentence, a line, and the items numbered 1, 2 and 3.

items.enonce_markdown:
The following code has three mistakes. ``` Shop

Welcome

We sell fresh fish

  1. Tilapia
  2. Catfish
    3. ``` Find the mistakes and write the corrected code.
items.solution_markdown:
The mistakes are: 1. The head is never closed: `` is missing before ``. 2. `` and `` cross each other: `` was opened last so it must be closed first, as in `fresh fish`. 3. The list is opened with `
    ` but closed with ``. The closing tag must match, so the list is closed with `
`, or opened with `
    ` if bullets are wanted. One corrected version, with a bulleted list, is: ``` Shop

    Welcome

    We sell fresh fish

    • Tilapia
    • Catfish
    ``` The browser shows **2 bullets**, one for Tilapia and one for Catfish.

items.enonce_markdown:
Write the HTML code for a page with all of these.

- The title *My Class* in the browser tab.
- A level 2 heading *Our subjects*.
- A bulleted list of Mathematics, Computer Science and English.
- A paragraph in which the word *Visit* is a link to https://www.example.com, followed by the words *our website.*
- A picture from the file school.jpg with the alternative text *Our school*.
- A table with two columns, *Subject* and *Periods* as headings, and one row of data: Mathematics and 5.

Then say how many bullets and how many table cells the browser will show.
items.solution_markdown:
One correct answer is: ``` My Class

Our subjects

  • Mathematics
  • Computer Science
  • English

Visit our website.

SubjectPeriods
Mathematics5
``` The browser shows **3 bullets** (one per `
  • `) and **4 table cells**: two heading cells (``) and two data cells (``), that is 2 rows x 2 cells. The `` tag is an empty tag, so it has no closing tag.
